g.text: Lab 02: Idempotent Write Architecture & Caching Lifecycle
Complete Distributed Topology: Node.js Express • Redis 7 Atomic Locks (SETNX) • Response Replay • Race Condition Guard
How requests move through atomic lock acquisition, response caching, instant replays, and conflict rejection
• Inserts order row into orders[] with ID = 1
• Stores JSON { status: 201, body } in Redis
Database mutation executes strictly once; final response
is saved in Redis to protect against future client retries.
Cause: Mobile timeout or network retry policy
Business logic & billing are completely bypassed;
the client receives the exact expected state immediately.
• Both hit the server at the exact same millisecond
detail: "Mutation In Progress. Please retry shortly."
Redis atomic operations guarantee mutual exclusion,
preventing double mutations across multi-core workers.
